chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad and Fadalah from Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala' said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who intends to perform Hajj: does he take (cut) from his hair during the entire month of Shawwal, provided he has not seen the crescent? He said, 'Yes, there is no harm in it.'

key_terms.مَا لَمْ: provided that not / as long as

ai.seo_question: When can a pilgrim cut their hair before Hajj if the moon hasn't been seen yet?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise temporal boundary for the prohibition of grooming (cutting hair and nails) for a Muhrim, establishing that the restriction commences only upon the sighting of the Dhu al-Hijjah crescent rather than a fixed calendar date. It highlights the Shia scholarly reliance on lunar sighting (*ru'yah*) to determine the start of the Hajj season, ensuring that pilgrims remain in a state of permissibility for personal grooming until the specific ritual marker is confirmed.
